title: Sweden after the gold standard: the consumer price index, annual, 1925-1939
source: Sveriges riksbank, Historical Monetary and Financial Statistics for Sweden: Volume I, ch. 8 (R. Edvinsson and J. Soederberg, 'The evolution of Swedish consumer prices, 1290-2008', 2010), Table I.A8.1 'A Consumer Price Index for Sweden 1290-' (file volym1/volumeich8consumerpriceindex.xls, version 2.1); Volume II, ch. 6 (D. Waldenstroem, 'Swedish stock and bond returns, 1856-2012', 2014), Table II.A6.9 (file volym2/volumeiich6stocksandbonds.xls, version 2.0)
series: year; cpi_1914_100: Table I.A8.1, 'Deflation index 1914 = 100' (the printed table says July 1914 = 100), an annual index
license: Sveriges riksbank's terms for its open data: 'The Riksbank's open data is freely available and may be further used without any special consent or agreement being required. Enter source, Sveriges riksbank and date. If you have processed statistics taken from the Riksbank's website, you may not state Sveriges Riksbank as the source.' The snapshot stores the values as published (source: Sveriges riksbank, 2026-10-22). The index on the base 1931 = 100 and the changes the chapter computes from them are the book's own calculations and are attributed to the book and to Edvinsson and Soederberg (2010) and Waldenstroem (2014), not to the Riksbank.
notes: An annual index, not the weekly or monthly consumer price index the Riksbank computed from the autumn of 1931 for its programme (Berg and Jonung 1998, row bj98_weekly of alternatives_facts), whose base was September 1931 = 100. The chapter rebases this annual index to 1931 = 100 for its figure; the band of 'less than 3 percentage points' in Berg and Jonung refers to the Riksbank's own index, not to this one. The same file gives the values to 1913 used by Chapter 25 (riksbank_sweden_1870_1913).
citation: Edvinsson, R. and J. Soederberg (2010), 'The evolution of Swedish consumer prices, 1290-2008', and Waldenstroem, D. (2014), 'Swedish stock and bond returns, 1856-2012', in R. Edvinsson, T.
